Kherwar is the Santals' own ancestral self-description, so the movement was addressed to the community as a community; Sapha Har means the clean or pure people, which is what its followers set out to become. In practice that meant turning away from the many bongas or spirits and the animal sacrifices offered to them, worshipping a single supreme being instead, and reforming conduct within Santal society. Both halves of option (b) describe it.

question: In which one of the following years was the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha established?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1870. The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was founded in 1870 at Poona, with Mahadev Govind Ranade as its intellectual force and Ganesh Vasudev Joshi among its organisers. It was one of the earliest bodies in India to claim to speak for a public rather than for a caste, a sect or a princely interest: the word sarvajanik in its name means precisely 'of all the people', and it worked by collecting evidence, drafting memorials and petitioning. Its best-remembered act came five years later, in 1875, when it sent a petition signed by tens of thousands of Indians to the House of Commons asking for direct Indian representation in the British Parliament. That 1875 date is what makes option (b), 1876, and option (a), 1884, so tempting.

question: Which one of the following was an important Pandya port, celebrated for its pearls in Sangam poems and Greek accounts?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Korkai. Korkai lay near the mouth of the Thamirabarani on the Gulf of Mannar, in what is now Thoothukudi district, and it is the port the Sangam poems and the Greek accounts both name for its pearls. The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, a Greek merchant's handbook of the first century, puts it beyond words: 'From Comari toward the south this region extends to Colchi, where the pearl-fisheries are ... and it belongs to the Pandian Kingdom.' Colchi is Korkai, Comari is Cape Comorin, and the Pandian Kingdom is the Pandyas. Tamil tradition remembers Korkai as an early Pandya seat before Madurai, and the pearl banks of the Gulf of Mannar are the reason the port existed at all. Silt has since pushed the coastline several kilometres away, so the site now lies inland.

question: The town of Chisht, from which the Sufi Chishti Silsila derives its name, is located in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Central Afghanistan. Sufi orders take their names in two ways: some from their founding figure, as the Qadiri order does from Shaikh Abd'ul Qadir Jilani, and some from a place. The Chishtis are of the second kind. NCERT states the point in as many words: some orders 'were named after their place of origin, in this case the town of Chisht in central Afghanistan'. The town, Chisht-e Sharif, lies in the valley of the Hari Rud in Herat province, on the western edge of the Afghan highlands, and the order carried its name into India with the migration of Sufis in the late twelfth century. Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti settled at Ajmer, and the silsila became the most influential in the subcontinent.

question: The rules for congregational worship (Sangat) involving collective recitation were organized by
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Guru Nanak. The stem is taken almost word for word from the standard textbook account: 'Baba Guru Nanak organised his followers into a community. He set up rules for congregational worship (sangat) involving collective recitation.' Nanak's teaching was that the Divine has no gender or form and is approached by remembering and repeating the Divine Name, and he expressed it in hymns called shabad, composed in Punjabi and sung in various ragas while his companion Mardana played the rabab. Turning that practice into a rule for a gathered community (a sangat meeting to recite together) is what the question is pointing at, and it was Nanak who did it, at Kartarpur in his last years. He also appointed his disciple Angad to succeed him as guru, and the succession ran for nearly two centuries.

question: Who amongst the following will be at more risk with respect to the earthquake hazard zone specified by the Geological Survey of India?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Malti at Pithoragarh. Of the four places named, only Pithoragarh sits on the Himalayan front , where the Indian plate is being driven under Eurasia along a stack of thrusts and where the country's largest earthquakes occur. Uttarakhand government disaster-management material places the district in Zone V , the highest category on the Indian zoning map. The other three lie in the stable peninsular interior. The code lists Hyderabad, the twin city of Secunderabad, in Zone II and Bhubaneswar in Zone III; Indore is not listed, but Madhya Pradesh's listed towns sit in Zones II and III. So the ranking is unambiguous even before the exact zone number for Pithoragarh is settled.

question: The Government wants to prepare a plan for drought prone areas of the country. Which one of the following regions will be predominantly focused?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Kutch region. Drought planning targets the parts of the country where rainfall is both low and unreliable, and Kutch is the driest inhabited tract in India outside the Thar. Under the Koeppen scheme used in the school geography, north-western Gujarat falls in the semi-arid steppe type BShw, sitting immediately alongside the hot desert type of extreme western Rajasthan; annual rainfall is small, it falls in a few weeks, and the year-to-year variability is high, which is what turns low rainfall into recurrent drought. Add saline soils and the salt flats of the Great and Little Rann, and Kutch is exactly the terrain that drought-prone area programmes were designed for. None of the other three regions is arid.

question: Four persons are travelling to different States of India. To whom will you advise to protect oneself from blizzards?
opt_a: The person travelling to Arunachal Pradesh
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, The person travelling to Arunachal Pradesh. A blizzard needs three things at once: falling or already fallen snow, a strong wind to lift and drive it, and the low visibility that results. That combination requires high, cold, snow-covered country, and of the four States named only Arunachal Pradesh has it. The State sits in the Eastern Himalaya and rises to Kangto at 7,090 metres on the border with Tibet; its high passes and upper valleys, Sela and the Tawang country among them, hold snow through the winter and are regularly closed by snow and wind. The other three lie at low elevation in a humid subtropical or tropical setting where snow does not fall at all.

question: Which one of the following States is not prominent for plantation agriculture?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Rajasthan. Plantation agriculture means a single cash crop grown on a large estate, capital-intensive, worked by hired labour, and grown for a market and usually for a processing industry: tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane, banana and spices are the Indian examples. Every one of those crops needs plentiful and dependable water, and most need warm humid conditions and often a slope with good drainage. Rajasthan has none of that: the west is arid and semi-arid, the state's characteristic crops are bajra, jowar, pulses, oilseeds such as mustard, and it is known instead for pastoralism and dryland farming. Assam is the country's principal tea region, Kerala grows rubber, spices, coffee and coconut on plantations, and Nagaland has tea and rubber holdings in its hills; Rajasthan is the outlier.

question: The distance between which two cities has been reduced by the Atal Tunnel?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Manali to Leh. The Atal Tunnel runs under the Rohtang pass in Himachal Pradesh, carrying the Manali-Leh road through the eastern Pir Panjal instead of over it. It is 9.02 kilometres long, was built by the Border Roads Organisation, and was inaugurated on 3 October 2020, having been renamed after Atal Bihari Vajpayee in 2019. The gain is both distance and dependability. The Manali-Keylong stretch falls from about 116 kilometres by the old route over Rohtang to about 71 kilometres, cutting several hours off the journey. More importantly, the Lahaul valley no longer loses its road link for months each winter when the pass closes. That year-round access to the first leg of the Manali-Leh road is why the tunnel matters strategically as well as commercially .

question: Which one of the following biosphere reserves comprises islands with estuaries, beaches, coral reefs, salt marshes and mangroves?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Gulf of Mannar biosphere reserve. The description in the stem is a list of coastal habitats gathered around islands, and that is the Gulf of Mannar's defining feature: a chain of twenty-one uninhabited islands strung between Rameswaram and Tuticorin along the Tamil Nadu coast, with coral reefs, seagrass beds and mangroves around them and estuaries, beaches and salt marshes on the adjoining shore. Those islands and the reefs around them were declared a Marine National Park in 1986 and the wider area a biosphere reserve in 1989; UNESCO added it to the World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2001 and describes it as one of the world's richest regions from a marine biodiversity point of view. It is also the flagship habitat of the dugong in Indian waters.

question: Which one of the following is not a correct statement with reference to the Constitution of India?
opt_a: The Constitution (Eighty-Fifth) Amendment Act has inserted the 'Right to Education' under Article 21A.
opt_c: Right to Constitutional Remedies is in Part-III of the Constitution.
opt_d: Writ jurisdiction of High Courts is wider than the Supreme Court of India.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, The Constitution (Eighty-Fifth) Amendment Act has inserted the 'Right to Education' under Article 21A. That is the statement that is wrong, and in a stem asking which is not correct it is therefore the answer. Article 21A was inserted by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, which also substituted Article 45 to direct the State towards early childhood care for children below six and added the fundamental duty in Article 51A(k); the article itself was brought into force on 1 April 2010 alongside the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. The Eighty-fifth Amendment Act, 2001 did something quite different: it amended Article 16(4A) to allow reservation in promotion with consequential seniority for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and it did so retrospectively. The other three statements in the question are accurate.

question: Which one of the following statements about the Cripps Mission is not correct?
opt_a: It was sent to India by the British Government in March 1942.
opt_b: It proposed that the Constitution of India was to be framed by an elected Constituent Assembly of the Indian people.
opt_c: Any province which was not prepared to accept the Constitution would be free to retain its constitutional provisions existing at that time.
opt_d: The British Government could enter into a separate constitutional arrangement with any of the acceding provinces.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, The British Government could enter into a separate constitutional arrangement with any of the acceding provinces. The word to catch is acceding. The Draft Declaration published on 30 March 1942 offered the separate arrangement to provinces that did not accede, not to those that did. Its clause (c)(i) gives 'the right of any Province of British India that is not prepared to accept the new Constitution to retain its present constitutional position, provision being made for its subsequent accession if it so decides', and then continues: 'With such non-acceding Provinces, should they so desire, His Majesty's Government will be prepared to agree upon a new Constitution, giving them the same full status as the Indian Union.' A province that acceded would be inside the new Constitution and would have no need of an arrangement of its own. The other three statements are accurate as printed.

question: Which of the following statements regarding constitutional amendment is/are correct? 1. The procedure for amendment to the Constitution is provided in Article 368. 2. A Bill to amend the Constitution can be introduced in either House of the Parliament. 3. The special procedure in Article 368 vests constituent powers upon the ordinary legislation. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1, 2 and 3. Statement 1 is the easy one: Article 368 , in Part XX of the Constitution, is headed 'Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor', and it is the only article that lays down an amending procedure. Statement 2 is the text of Article 368(2) itself: an amendment 'may be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either House of Parliament'. Statement 3 is where candidates stall. There is no separate constituent assembly for amendments; the same two Houses that pass ordinary laws become the amending authority, but only when they follow the heavier route of Article 368. That is what it means to say the special procedure vests constituent power in the ordinary legislature , and the 24th Amendment of 1971 wrote 'in exercise of its constituent power' into Article 368(1) to put the point beyond argument.

question: Which one of the following is not a circumstance for proclamation of Emergency by the President of India under Article 352 of the Constitution of India?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Internal disturbance. Article 352(1) lets the President proclaim a National Emergency when satisfied that a grave emergency exists whereby the security of India or of any part of its territory is threatened, 'whether by war or external aggression or armed rebellion'. Those three, and only those three, are the grounds now written into the article, so war, external aggression and armed rebellion all belong in the list and internal disturbance does not. It used to. The Constitution as adopted in 1950 read 'internal disturbance' where 'armed rebellion' now stands, and the Emergency proclaimed in June 1975 was made on precisely that ground. The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 replaced the loose phrase with the far narrower 'armed rebellion' and hardened the procedure around it, so that a disturbance falling short of armed rebellion can no longer support a proclamation under Article 352. The wording that was removed is the option the paper wants you to spot.

question: Akbar issued a Farman in 1598 permitting in the city of Cambay (Khambat), Gujarat, the construction of a
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Church. The beneficiaries of the 1598 order were the Jesuits , and what they were asking permission for at the port of Cambay was a house of prayer of their own. By that date the Society of Jesus had been at Akbar's court for eighteen years across three missions: the first arrived at Fatehpur Sikri in 1580, a second followed in 1591, and the third, led by Jerome Xavier, reached Lahore on 5 May 1595 and stayed on in Mughal service until 1614. Akbar had already given the fathers ground at Agra on which a church was raised, and he granted Xavier a farman guaranteeing freedom of worship to Christians when the mission's position looked unsafe. Cambay explains the location: it was Gujarat's great ocean port , where Portuguese shipping and Jesuit personnel entered Mughal territory, and the fathers of the earlier missions had been received there on their way inland.

question: Domingo Paes, the medieval traveller, has described the city of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Vijayanagara. Domingo Paes was a Portuguese who travelled inland from Goa with traders around 1520 and left the fullest European description we have of the Vijayanagara capital, in the chronicle of the kings of Bisnaga. He saw the city in the reign of Krishnadeva Raya, at the height of its power, and what struck him was its size and its greenery: his account says that from a hill he could see only part of it, that what he saw seemed to him as large as Rome and very beautiful to the sight, and that there were many groves of trees within it, many conduits of water flowing into the middle of it, and lakes. He also described the huge tank Krishnadeva Raya built, fed by water brought from more than three leagues away through pipes. Paes belongs to a small group of foreign visitors whose accounts historians lean on for this city, alongside Abdur Razzaq of Persia and Nicolo de' Conti and Afanasii Nikitin in the previous century, and his fellow Portuguese Duarte Barbosa and Fernao Nuniz.

question: The extent of damage caused by earthquake is not influenced by which one of the following?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Climate of the area. Damage from an earthquake is the product of three separate things: how hard the ground shakes, how much is standing in the way of that shaking, and how well the things standing there resist it. Strength of the earthquake covers the first: magnitude measures the energy released, and intensity, on the Modified Mercalli scale, measures the shaking and destruction felt at a place. Population density covers the second, which is why casualty figures track settlement and not magnitude alone. Type of building covers the third, and it is the factor engineers say matters most. Climate does not enter that chain : a given ground motion under a given building does the same thing to it in a hot dry plain as in a cold wet one.

question: An avalanche is a type of which one of the following disasters?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Terrestrial. An avalanche is a rapid flow of snow down a slope, which as it grows can pick up and carry ice, rock, soil and trees with it. That makes it a mass movement of material along the land surface under gravity (the same family as a landslide, a rockfall or a mudflow) and disaster classifications that sort events by the sphere they occur in put all of these together as terrestrial. The sorting rule is where the event happens, not what set it off. Atmospheric disasters are events of the air itself: cyclones, hailstorms, thunderstorms, frost, drought. Aquatic ones happen in water bodies: floods, tsunamis, storm surges. Biological ones involve living agents: epidemics and pest attacks. Snow sliding off a mountainside sits in none of those three; it is material moving on land, so it is terrestrial.

question: An infection constantly maintained at a baseline level in a geographic area without external input is known as
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Endemic. In epidemiology an infection is called endemic when it is constantly present, or maintained at a baseline level, in a given population or geographic area: the case numbers are steady and predictable, and they stay that way without being topped up from outside. The condition behind that steadiness is easy to state: for a disease spread person to person, the basic reproduction number multiplied by the proportion of the population still susceptible has to sit at one, so that each infection replaces itself exactly and the infection neither dies out nor grows exponentially. The wording of the stem (a baseline level, in a geographic area, without external input) is that definition almost word for word. The other three options all describe departures from the steady state rather than the steady state itself.

question: Streams and rivers coming from the mountains deposit heavy materials of rocks and boulders in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Bhabar. Where the Himalayan streams leave the mountains and hit the sudden break of slope at the foot of the Shiwaliks, their velocity collapses, and the first material they can no longer carry is the heaviest: rocks, boulders and coarse pebbles. That deposition builds a narrow porous belt of about eight to ten kilometres running parallel to the Shiwalik foothills, called the bhabar . The belt is so coarse and permeable that the smaller streams sink into it and vanish underground, to re-emerge a little further south.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the electoral rolls is/are correct? 1. There is one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency. 2. No person is ineligible for inclusion in the electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or any of them. 3. A citizen of India, not less than 18 years of age, can cast his/her vote unless disqualified under a law of an appropriate legislature. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1, 2 and 3. All three statements are drawn from two short articles of the Constitution. Article 325 supplies the first two in one sentence. It provides one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency for elections to either House of Parliament or a State legislature, and says no person is ineligible for inclusion in it, or may claim inclusion in any special roll, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or any of them. That clause abolished the separate communal electorates of the colonial period. Article 326 supplies the third: elections to the Lok Sabha and State legislative assemblies are on the basis of adult suffrage, and every citizen not less than eighteen years of age on the qualifying date, and not otherwise disqualified under the Constitution or a law made by the appropriate legislature, is entitled to be registered as a voter.

question: Which one of the following statements is not correct about ‘Totalitarianism’?
opt_a: It is not akin to autocracy and authoritarianism.
opt_b: It usurps political freedom of the individuals, but it doesn’t usurp personal freedoms.
opt_c: It implies abolition of civil society.
opt_d: It is usually identified with a one-party state.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, It usurps political freedom of the individuals, but it doesn't usurp personal freedoms. That statement fails on the point that defines the term. A totalitarian system does not stop at politics: working from an official dominant ideology, it reaches into the economy, education, the arts and sciences, and the private morality of citizens. It holds that reach in place with censorship of every channel of mass communication, mass surveillance and terror; the word itself was coined to describe a state claiming the whole of life . A system that took political freedom away and left private life alone would be called authoritarian , not totalitarian, because authoritarian rule is concerned with political power and leaves society a certain measure of liberty. Statement (b) attaches the authoritarian description to the totalitarian label.

question: Who among the following was chosen for the Kuvempu Award 2020?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Dr. Rajendra Kishore Panda. The Kuvempu Rashtriya Puraskar for 2020 went to the Odia poet and novelist Rajendra Kishore Panda, who was born in 1944 in Sambalpur district and took his master's degree at the University of Allahabad. He was already among the most decorated writers in Odia, with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1985 for the poetry collection Shailakalpa, a D.Litt from Sambalpur University in 2004 and the Gangadhar National Award in 2010. He published some sixteen collections of verse along with fiction, including the novel Chidabhas, and he died in 2025. The award is a national literary honour named after Kuvempu and given to a writer in any Indian language , which is how a Kannada memorial prize comes to be won by an Odia poet.

question: Avani Lekhara became the first Indian woman to win two Paralympics medals at the Tokyo Paralympics 2020. Which one of the following was her discipline?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Shooting. Avani Lekhara is a para rifle shooter in the SH1 classification, and at the Tokyo Paralympic Games she won two medals in that sport: gold in the women's 10 metre air rifle standing SH1, set with a Paralympic record of 249.6 in the final, and bronze in the 50 metre rifle three positions SH1. The gold was the first ever won by an Indian woman at the Paralympic Games, and the pair of medals at a single Games is what the stem is referring to. She comes from Jaipur in Rajasthan and took up shooting after a road accident in 2012 left her paraplegic; the recognition that followed included the Khel Ratna in 2021 and the Padma Shri in 2022. Since this paper was set she has gone further still, defending the 10 metre air rifle standing SH1 title at the Paris Paralympic Games in 2024.

question: Bagram Air Base is located in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Afghanistan. Bagram Airfield lies in Parwan province, about eleven kilometres south-east of Charikar and some forty kilometres from Kabul. The Soviet Union built it in the 1950s, and after 2001 it became the largest American and NATO base in the country: the logistics hub, detention centre and air operations base around which the whole western military presence turned. That is why its handover was read as the real end of the war rather than a stage in it: American forces left Bagram on the night of 1 to 2 July 2021, shutting off the power and departing without informing the incoming Afghan commander, and on 15 August 2021, as Kabul fell, the Afghan troops holding it withdrew and the Taliban took the base along with the thousands of prisoners held there. This paper was set in November 2021, with all of that a few months old, which is exactly why the base was in the question.

question: The Panchmuli Lake is situated near
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Statue of Unity. Panchmuli Lake lies inside the Statue of Unity tourism complex at Kevadia, now renamed Ekta Nagar, in Narmada district of Gujarat. It is one of the dykes of the Sardar Sarovar project on the Narmada, developed as an eco-tourism water body with boat rides that run out across it into forested country under the Vindhya hills. The Statue of Unity is a 182-metre figure of Vallabhbhai Patel standing on Sadhu Bet island in the Narmada, facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam, sculpted by Ram V. Sutar and inaugurated on 31 October 2018. Of the four monuments listed, it is the only one anywhere near the Narmada .

question: Pinaka, developed in India, is a
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, multi-barrel rocket launcher. Pinaka is a multiple launch rocket system built for the Indian Army by the Defence Research and Development Organisation, with the Armament Research and Development Establishment as the system coordinator. A single launcher vehicle carries twelve rockets and can put all twelve into the air in about forty-four seconds, which is what a rocket artillery system is for: saturating an area target in one burst rather than engaging a point target with a single round. It went into action before it was formally in service, firing in June 1999 during the Kargil conflict, and the first Pinaka regiment was raised in February 2000. The system has been improved steadily since: the original Mark I reaches about 37.5 kilometres, an enhanced Mark I about 45, the Mark II about 60, and the guided version between 75 and 80. The name is taken from the bow of Shiva.

question: What is itat e-dwar?
opt_a: An Urdu magazine published from Lucknow
opt_b: An e-filing portal of Income Tax Appellate Tribunal
opt_d: Name of a UNESCO world heritage site
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, An e-filing portal of Income Tax Appellate Tribunal. The portal named itat e-dwar was launched on 25 June 2021 by the Union Minister for Law and Justice, Ravi Shankar Prasad, at a virtual function attended by tribunal functionaries from all twenty-eight stations along with bar associations, income tax officers and chartered accountants. It lets parties file appeals, miscellaneous applications, documents and paper books electronically instead of physically, and it was presented as raising accessibility, accountability and transparency in the tribunal's day-to-day working. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal itself is an old institution: set up on 25 January 1941, it was the first experiment in tribunalisation in India, and it functions under the Department of Legal Affairs in the Ministry of Law and Justice, deliberately kept apart from the Ministry of Finance so that the forum hearing tax appeals is not answerable to the department collecting the tax.

question: What is the range capability of Agni-P Ballistic Missile?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 1,000 – 2,000 km. Agni-P, also called Agni Prime, is the sixth missile of the Agni series and is described by its developers as covering 1,000 to 2,000 kilometres with a payload of about 1.5 tonnes. It was flight-tested for the first time on 28 June 2021 from the Integrated Test Range, five months before this paper was written, which is why the range figure was fresh enough to ask about. The design is a two-stage solid-fuelled road-mobile ballistic missile carried in a sealed twin canister, so it travels by road or rail already mated with its warhead and needs very little preparation before launch, and it carries a manoeuvring re-entry vehicle. In the family it is the replacement at the short end: lighter than Agni-III and built with technologies proved on Agni-IV and Agni-V, but intended to take over the role of the older Agni-I and Agni-II rather than to reach further than them.

question: Which one of the following Indian States has recently declared itself as the first rabies-free State?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Goa. In June 2021 Goa became the first Indian state to be declared a rabies-controlled area, and on 23 June 2021 the Chief Minister, Pramod Sawant, announced that Goa had become India's first rabies-free state. The achievement rests on a decade of work by the state government with the Mission Rabies programme, built on the mass vaccination of dogs (of the order of ninety thousand a year across the state) together with community education, a surveillance and bite-response network and a hotline for reporting suspected cases. The result that matters is that Goa has recorded no human death from rabies since 2018, an elimination later documented in the peer-reviewed literature as a One Health success, meaning it was achieved by treating animal health, human health and the environment as one problem rather than three.

question: Department of Public Enterprises is a part of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Ministry of Finance. The Department of Public Enterprises is the nodal department for central public sector enterprises, and until the middle of 2021 it sat where its name suggests, inside the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises alongside the Department of Heavy Industry. In July 2021 it was moved to the Ministry of Finance, and the parent ministry was renamed simply the Ministry of Heavy Industries on 7 July 2021 to reflect the loss. That transfer is what made the question askable four months later. The logic behind it is not hard to see: the questions that dominate public sector policy now (disinvestment, strategic sale, asset monetisation and the return the state gets on the capital locked up in these companies) are financial questions, and the Ministry of Finance already houses the machinery for them. The Ministry of Heavy Industries kept the administration of the engineering and automobile sector and the public enterprises that belong to it.

question: Chronologically arrange the following Indian-origin astronauts on the basis of their flying into space starting with the first: 1. Sunita Williams 2. Rakesh Sharma 3. Sirisha Bandla 4. Kalpana Chawla Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 2-4-1-3. Taking the four in the order they first left the ground: Rakesh Sharma flew on 3 April 1984 aboard Soyuz T-11 to the Salyut 7 station, spending seven days and about twenty-two hours in orbit as the first Indian in space. Kalpana Chawla followed in 1997 as a mission specialist on Space Shuttle flight STS-87, the first woman of Indian origin to fly. Sunita Williams launched on 9 December 2006 aboard Space Shuttle Discovery on STS-116, joining the Expedition 14 crew on the International Space Station. Sirisha Bandla was the most recent of the four, flying on 11 July 2021 on Virgin Galactic's Unity 22 suborbital flight to about ninety kilometres. So the sequence runs Rakesh Sharma, Kalpana Chawla, Sunita Williams, Sirisha Bandla: statement 2, then 4, then 1, then 3.

question: President Jovenel Moise, who was assassinated recently, was the President of which one of the following countries?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Haiti. Jovenel Moise was the forty-eighth President of Haiti, a businessman before he entered politics, and he was shot dead in the early hours of 7 July 2021 when armed men attacked his private residence at Pelerin 5, in the Petion-Ville district above Port-au-Prince. He was fifty-three. His wife Martine was wounded in the attack and was flown to Miami for treatment; their three children were unhurt. The acting prime minister at the time said the attackers included men speaking Spanish, and the investigation that followed produced indictments over the next several years, including of the president's widow and of the acting prime minister, one of which was later overturned on appeal. The killing left Haiti without a functioning presidency and deepened a political crisis that has continued since.

question: Recently, which one among the following Ministries was formed under the Government of India?
opt_a: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
opt_b: Ministry of Development of North-Eastern Region
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Ministry of Cooperation. The Ministry of Cooperation was created on 6 July 2021, and Amit Shah took charge of it as its first Cabinet Minister the following day, holding the portfolio alongside Home Affairs. The Finance Minister had announced the intention to set up a separate administrative structure for cooperatives in the Union budget presented earlier that year, and the new ministry took over work that had until then been done inside the Ministry of Agriculture. Its stated purpose is to give the cooperative sector a separate administrative, legal and policy framework, strengthen cooperatives at the grassroots and streamline the working of multi-state cooperative societies, under the motto sahkar se samriddhi, prosperity through cooperation. Being four months old when this paper was written, it was the obvious answer.

question: Indian Naval Ship INS Tabar had recently participated in a two-day naval exercise with the Italian Navy. The exercise was conducted in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Tyrrhenian Sea. INS Tabar, a Talwar-class frigate commissioned in April 2004, spent the summer of 2021 on a long deployment to Europe, and on 4 and 5 July 2021 it exercised with the Italian Navy frigate ITS Antonio Marceglia in the Tyrrhenian Sea: the arm of the Mediterranean enclosed by mainland Italy, Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica. The two ships worked through air defence drills, replenishment at sea, communication exercises and cross-deck helicopter operations by day and by night, which is the standard content of a short bilateral passage exercise. The same deployment took the ship on to the Bay of Biscay for an exercise with the French frigate FNS Aquitaine on 15 and 16 July, and then to St Petersburg for Russian Navy Day and Exercise INDRA in the Baltic at the end of the month: three navies in four weeks, which was the point of sending her.

question: Which one of the following countries has recently been awarded a malaria-free certification by the WHO?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, China. The World Health Organization certified China malaria-free on 30 June 2021, five months before this paper was set. The scale of what was undone is the striking part: China was reporting something like thirty million malaria cases a year in the 1940s, and it worked the number down over seven decades of sustained effort before recording its first year with no indigenous case. Certification is not awarded for low numbers. WHO grants it only when a country can prove that the chain of indigenous malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes has been broken nationwide for at least the previous three consecutive years, and can also show it has the surveillance and response capacity to stop the disease being re-established. At the time of China's certification about forty countries and territories had reached that standard.

question: Who amongst the following was honoured with Gandhi Peace Prize for the year 2020?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. The Gandhi Peace Prize for 2020 was conferred on Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the founding leader of Bangladesh, and it was given posthumously: he was assassinated in 1975. The citation followed the terms of the award, which honours contributions towards social, economic and political transformation through non-violent and other Gandhian methods. The timing mattered as much as the name: 2020 and 2021 were the years of the centenary of his birth and the fiftieth anniversary of Bangladesh's independence, and the award was one of a series of Indian gestures marking them.

question: Why was Dholavira in the news recently?
opt_c: For the discovery of gold and precious stones at this site
opt_d: It received the UNESCO World Heritage Tag
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, It received the UNESCO World Heritage Tag. Dholavira, a Harappan city in Kutch, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on 27 July 2021 , four months before this paper was written, which is what put it in the news. What makes it exceptional, and what the inscription rests on, is water . In a place with almost no rainfall the Harappans cut and built sixteen or more reservoirs of varying size, the largest of them carved to about seven metres deep and seventy-nine metres long, and fed them from seasonal streams through a system of dams and drains.

question: Which one of the following is the oldest football tournament of Asia?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Durand Cup. The Durand Cup was started in 1888 and is the oldest existing club football tournament in Asia; on the world list only four national competitions are older, which makes it the fifth oldest football competition anywhere. It was founded by Sir Henry Mortimer Durand, foreign secretary of the British Raj from 1884 to 1894, who set it up while recovering from illness at Shimla, and it was played there in its early years before moving on to Delhi and later to Kolkata. That founder's name should ring a second bell, because the same Mortimer Durand negotiated the boundary between British India and Afghanistan that still carries his name: one man is behind both the Durand Line and the Durand Cup, which is a useful hook for two different questions.

question: Who among the following is the first Indian woman to win a medal in the Olympics?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Karnam Malleswari. Karnam Malleswari won the bronze medal in the women's 69 kilogram weightlifting event at the Sydney Olympic Games in 2000, lifting 110 kilograms in the snatch and 130 in the clean and jerk for a total of 240. It was the first Olympic medal ever won by an Indian woman, and it was also the only medal India took home from those Games. The event mattered for a second reason: women's weightlifting was contested at the Olympics for the first time at Sydney, so she was among the first group of women in the world to win an Olympic medal in the sport. Every other name in the list belongs to a later generation or to a fourth place, which is what the question is checking.

question: The Russian Federation participated in the Tokyo Olympics, 2020 under which of the following names?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Russian Olympic Committee. Russian athletes competed at the Tokyo Games under the designation ROC, standing for Russian Olympic Committee, and under that committee's flag rather than the national one. The reason lies in doping. The World Anti-Doping Agency banned Russia on 9 December 2019 for four years after finding that anti-doping laboratory data had been manipulated; on 17 December 2020 the Court of Arbitration for Sport reduced the penalty to two years and defined it as a bar on the use of the Russian name, flag and anthem, while allowing uniforms to carry the word Russia and the national colours. A fragment of Tchaikovsky's First Piano Concerto stood in for the anthem, approved by the International Olympic Committee on 22 April 2021 after an earlier proposal had been rejected. Competing in that form, the ROC finished fifth on the table with twenty gold, twenty-eight silver and twenty-three bronze: seventy-one medals in all.

question: Which of the following States/Union Territory/Region are in special focus in the National Mission on Edible Oils—Oil Palm?
opt_a: Himachal Pradesh and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
opt_b: North-East Region and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, North-East Region and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm was announced by the Prime Minister in the Independence Day address of 2021 and approved by the Union Cabinet on 18 August 2021, three months before this paper was set. The special focus written into the scheme is on the north-eastern region and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands . The reason is agronomic rather than political: oil palm needs high and well-distributed rainfall and a humid tropical climate, and those two areas are where India's assessments put the largest untapped potential. Two design features carry the special focus: extra capital assistance for processing units set up in the north-east and the Andamans, and a viability gap payment that guarantees growers a price for their fresh fruit bunches when international crude palm oil prices fall.
